reads.source: Gallica f641, native IIIF (1915x3125), six column-height crops (both columns, three bands each), plus a 4x upscaled crop of col 1282A at the Hebrew word; archive.org p.646 rendered at 200 dpi over the right column. CALIBRATION PAGE: printed corners read FIRST and give 1281 / 1282.
reads.found: ONE plate/TEI divergence and one lost non-Latin type. (1) col 1282A: Migne sets HEBREW TYPE that our TEI drops entirely -- the plate reads 'Hebraice mesuchan (מסכן), quia genus ligni est imputribile' and our TEI reads 'Hebraice mesuchan , quia', with the orphaned space where the parenthesis stood. Confirmed on BOTH printings (archive p.646 sets the same four letters). Patch filed; the Hebrew was NOT inserted into the English alone. (2) col 1281B: the plate prints 'VERS. 4. --' and our TEI prints 'VERS. 4--', dropping the period; the English renders the plate. Otherwise the running text collates word for word against src/latin/8956/0020.md, including the ungrammatical 'nec ex creaturarum magnitudinem' at 1282B, which is Migne's. Vulgate divergences: Zach 8:7 quoted 'Ego congregabo populum orientis' for 'Ecce ego salvabo populum meum de terra orientis' (fired [var:]); the Gen. XXIV quotation 'Locutus est Sichen ad cor ejus' which stands nowhere in the Vulgate, cited to Gen. XXIV for Gen. 34 (fired [var:], citation reproduced verbatim); the VERS. 13 lemma conflating Is 61:1 without 'Dominus' with Is 11:2 (fired [var:]); Amos 3:6 in the present subjunctive (crux); Is 40:25 'adaequastis me' for 'adaequastis' (crux). Foot of both columns blank -- no numbered or asterisk conjecture.

reads.page: f642, with archive.org p.647 as second witness
reads.source: Gallica f642, native IIIF, six column-height crops, plus upscaled crops of col 1283A 'tunduntur.I' and col 1284D 'vestustate litterae'; archive.org p.647 rendered at 200 dpi over both of those lines. Printed corners read first: 1283 / 1284.
reads.found: NO plate/TEI divergence, and TWO sites where the two printings differ and NOTHING is marked. (1) col 1283A: Gallica sets 'saeculi tunduntur.I' -- a stray capital-I-shaped sort after the full stop, which our TEI also carries -- while archive p.647 prints 'tunduntur.' clean; a one-copy mark is not a public accusation against Migne's type, so no marker, no patch, and the English simply ends the sentence. (2) col 1284D: Gallica sets 'in vestustate litterae' (our TEI agrees) and archive p.647 sets 'vetustate' clean; same ruling, English reads 'in the oldness of the letter'. Confirmed as Migne's own, on the plate: the (Phil. II) / (Luc. I) citations at 1284B are printed exactly where our TEI has them, so the apparent swap is Migne's. Vulgate divergences: 1 Cor 15:31 'propter vestram gloriam' for 'per vestram gloriam' (fired [var:]); the second lemma at 1285A 'De vertice montis' singular against Is 42:11 'de vertice montium', the plural it had just quoted (fired [var:]); Is 41:1 'Taceant insulae' without 'ad me' (crux); Ps 21:7 without 'autem' (crux); Jo 9:39 word order 'ego veni in hunc mundum' (crux); Rom 11:25 'Cum plenitudo gentium intraverit' for 'donec ... intraret' (crux). reads.page: f645, with archive.org p.650 as second witness
reads.source: Gallica f645, native IIIF, six column-height crops, plus upscaled crops of col 1290A '(I Cor. x)', col 1290A 'ob oriente' and col 1290C 'Curavi- / vimus'; archive.org p.650 rendered at 200 dpi over all three. Printed corners read first: 1289 / 1290.
reads.found: ONE plate/TEI divergence, and TWO sites where the two printings differ and NOTHING is marked. (1) col 1290A: BOTH printings set '(I Cor. x)' with a single period, and our TEI carries '(I Cor.. X)' with a doubled point -- a digitization defect. Patch filed. (2) col 1290A: Gallica sets 'quem Magi ob oriente venientes adoraverunt' (our TEI agrees) and archive p.650 sets 'ab oriente' clean; one-copy defect, no marker, English reads 'coming from the east'. (3) col 1290C: Gallica hyphenates the Jer 51:9 lemma across the line as 'Curavi- / vimus Babylonem', i.e. Curavivimus (our TEI agrees), while archive p.650 sets 'Curavi- / mus', i.e. Curavimus, clean -- the archive column's left margin was measured against three neighbouring lines before this was recorded. One-copy defect, no marker, English reads 'We have healed Babylon'. Confirmed as Migne's on both printings: 'tempore Achaz et Ezechielis' at 1289D. Vulgate divergences: Ex 20:3 quoted 'Non erunt tibi dii alieni' for 'Non habebis deos alienos coram me' (fired [var:]); Is 45:21 'Praedixi illud' first person for 'praedixit illud' third (fired [var:]); Mt 2:1-2 conflated (crux); 1 Cor 10:11 recast as 'Nos sumus in quos ...' (crux); the (Psal. XXXV) citation attached to Is 45:9 at 1288C (crux, reproduced verbatim). Foot of col 1289 carries the running signature PATROL. CXIII.; foot of col 1290 the signature 41. No numbered or asterisk conjecture on either.
